channel.title: Payroll on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Payroll on Best of AI

item.title: Deputy
item.description:
Deputy is workforce management software for businesses with shift workers. Managers create schedules in a drag and drop calendar, publish them to staff, and employees see shifts in a mobile app where they can swap, pick up open shifts, or declare availability. Time clocks record when people arrive, and the data feeds payroll.

Compliance and cost control are big parts of the pitch. Deputy flags overtime and break rule violations based on local labor laws, forecasts labor needs against sales, and helps keep spending on target. Communication tools allow announcements and tasks, and integrations connect to payroll and point of sale systems.

item.title: Justworks
item.description:
Justworks is aimed at small companies that don’t want to run HR in house. The platform handles payroll, tax filings, benefits enrollment, time off, onboarding, and compliance in a single system, with a mobile app for employees. Its HR support team helps with questions about employment rules.

The distinct feature is the co-employment model. Justworks operates as a professional employer organization, which means it becomes a co-employer for tax and insurance purposes, pooling its customers to buy group health insurance and workers compensation at rates a small firm could not get alone. The business keeps day-to-day control over its staff and hiring.

item.title: Paychex
item.description:
Paychex is one of the largest payroll providers in the United States. Businesses use it to pay employees, file payroll taxes, manage time and attendance, administer retirement and health benefits, and handle HR tasks such as onboarding and compliance. A defining feature is access to human specialists, which suits owners who do not want to figure out payroll rules on their own.

The Paychex Flex platform pulls these services into one system with mobile apps for employees and managers. AI features assist with answering HR questions, flagging payroll errors, and analyzing workforce data. The company also offers professional employer organization services, in which it co-employs workers and takes on benefits and compliance responsibilities. It acquired Paycor, a provider of HR and payroll software, to move further into mid-sized businesses.

item.title: Paycom
item.description:
Paycom is an HR and payroll platform built on one database for all functions. Employers manage hiring, onboarding, time and attendance, payroll, benefits, performance, and learning in a unified system, so data entered once appears everywhere. This design is meant to reduce errors from syncing separate tools.

Its best-known idea is Beti, which stands for Better Employee Transaction Interface. Employees review and approve their own timecards, expenses, and paid time off before payroll is run, which pushes corrections to the person who knows the data best and reduces payroll mistakes. Paycom has also added AI assistants for HR questions and tasks.

item.title: Paylocity
item.description:
Paylocity provides cloud HR and payroll software, primarily for mid-sized companies. Employers run payroll, manage benefits enrollment, track time and scheduling, handle onboarding and performance, and report on workforce data, all within one platform. A mobile app lets employees see pay stubs, request time off, and update details.

The company emphasizes employee experience and community features, such as company feeds, recognition, and surveys, in addition to core payroll. An AI assistant answers employee questions about pay, benefits, and company policy using the employer’s data, and helps managers and HR with drafting and analysis, which reduces the number of routine tickets.

item.title: Remote
item.description:
Remote is a global employment platform. A company that wants to hire someone in another country normally needs a legal entity there, which is slow and costly. With Remote as the employer of record, the worker is legally employed by Remote locally, while the company directs their daily work. Remote handles contracts, payroll, taxes, benefits, and statutory requirements.

The platform also supports contractors, offers tools for onboarding, expenses, and equipment, and provides local compliance knowledge across many countries. A global payroll product helps companies that already have entities coordinate payments, and AI features assist HR teams with questions and workflows. The company has built its own entities in many countries rather than relying on partners.

item.title: UKG
item.description:
UKG is a major provider of human capital management software. Employers use it to run payroll, track time and attendance, schedule shifts for hourly workers, manage benefits, hire, and develop employees. It is especially strong in industries with large hourly workforces such as retail, healthcare, and manufacturing, where scheduling and labor compliance are complex.

AI is woven into the products. Its assistant helps managers and employees answer questions and complete tasks, analytics predict turnover and scheduling needs, and tools suggest schedules that balance demand, cost, and employee preferences. The company has multiple product lines, including UKG Pro for larger organizations and UKG Ready for mid-sized companies.

item.title: Deel
item.description:
Deel is a global hiring and payments platform. A company that wants to employ someone in another country can use Deel as the employer of record, which means Deel holds the legal employment relationship locally and handles contracts, payroll, benefits, and taxes. It also manages contractors, with agreements and payments in many currencies.

Beyond employment, Deel has built an HR suite covering global payroll for companies with their own entities, benefits, equipment, time tracking, and immigration support. AI features review and generate contracts against local rules, answer compliance questions, and automate workflows, which reduces the research that cross-border hiring requires.

item.title: Gusto
item.description:
Gusto is built for employers without a dedicated HR department. A business adds its team, and Gusto calculates pay, withholds and files payroll taxes, and pays employees and contractors. Employees get pay stubs and benefits information in an app, and onboarding checklists collect forms and agreements from new hires.

The platform extends beyond payroll. It offers health insurance and retirement plan administration through partners, time tracking, hiring tools, and compliance support such as reminders and labor law guidance. AI features help flag likely filing errors, draft job descriptions and policies, and answer HR questions in plain language.

item.title: HiredScore
item.description:
HiredScore applies AI to the early stages of hiring. When applications arrive, it grades candidates against the requirements of the role, surfaces people who might be good fits, including past applicants and current employees, and helps recruiters focus on promising profiles first.

It integrates with applicant tracking systems and HR platforms, and Workday acquired the company to build AI into its talent products. Features include internal mobility recommendations, which help companies fill roles from within, and reporting to monitor process fairness and compliance.

item.title: Visier
item.description:
Visier gathers data from HR systems into a model built for workforce questions. HR teams and managers explore metrics such as turnover, hiring speed, diversity, and compensation, and see how they vary by team and over time. Prebuilt analyses save the effort of building reports from scratch.

AI predicts who may leave, models the effect of decisions, and answers questions in plain language through a virtual assistant. Planning tools support headcount and cost scenarios, and integrations pull data from systems such as Workday and SAP.

item.title: 15Five
item.description:
15Five helps organizations manage how people work and develop. Employees submit short weekly check-ins about priorities, progress, and morale, and managers review them and respond, which keeps a regular rhythm of communication. The platform includes performance reviews, goal and OKR tracking, one-on-one meeting agendas, recognition features, and engagement surveys to measure how employees feel.

AI is used to support managers. The system can summarize check-in responses and survey results, suggest coaching tips, help write review feedback, and flag potential issues like declining engagement or flight risk. Its Best-Self Management framework offers training for managers on developing teams. Reports give HR leaders a view of trends across teams.

item.title: 7shifts
item.description:
7shifts is built for the quirks of restaurant staffing. Managers create schedules based on forecast sales, availability, and labor targets, and publish them to a staff app where employees can see shifts, request swaps, and pick up open shifts. The goal is to keep enough people on the floor without overspending on wages.

The platform adds operations tools. A time clock tracks hours, compliance features flag overtime and break rules by location, tip pooling and distribution help with fair payouts, and team chat replaces scattered text threads. Integrations with point of sale systems provide sales data that feeds labor forecasts, and payroll exports reduce manual work.

item.title: ADP
item.description:
ADP is one of the best-known payroll companies in the world. It pays employees, files payroll taxes, and manages benefits administration, time and attendance, hiring, and HR records. Products range from simple small-business payroll to large, multi-country platforms for enterprises, and many companies outsource payroll entirely to ADP to ensure accuracy and compliance with changing tax rules.

Technology is increasingly part of the offering. ADP uses AI for assistants that answer HR and payroll questions, flag errors before payroll runs, and give managers insight into workforce trends, using its large dataset of payroll information to benchmark pay and turnover. The platform integrates with accounting and HR systems, and mobile apps let employees see pay stubs and request time off.

item.title: BambooHR
item.description:
BambooHR is built for companies without a large HR department. It keeps employee information in one place, tracks time off, handles onboarding checklists and documents, and offers an employee self-service portal. Applicant tracking helps with hiring, performance tools support reviews and goals, and payroll and benefits administration are available for U.S. customers. Reporting shows headcount, turnover, and other metrics.

The product is known for being easy to use, with a friendly interface and quick setup. AI features help HR teams with tasks such as drafting job descriptions and performance review language, summarizing feedback, and answering employee questions using company policies. Integrations connect with accounting, benefits, and productivity tools, and an app marketplace extends the platform.

item.title: Betterworks
item.description:
Betterworks supports how companies manage performance throughout the year. Employees set goals or OKRs that link to company priorities, managers hold regular check-ins, and feedback and recognition are captured along the way. Review cycles then draw on this record, so evaluations rely less on recent memory.

AI features help with the writing and analysis. An assistant can improve goal statements, summarize a year of feedback into review drafts, and suggest coaching points, while analytics show goal progress and engagement across teams. Integrations connect with HR systems like Workday and collaboration tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams.

item.title: CharlieHR
item.description:
CharlieHR is designed for companies without a dedicated HR team. It keeps employee records, tracks time off, runs onboarding checklists, stores contracts, and supports regular reviews and one-on-ones. The interface is simple, so small teams can adopt it without lengthy setup.

An AI assistant helps with everyday HR questions about policies and employment topics, and supports tasks such as drafting job descriptions or other documents. Integrations connect with payroll providers, so data does not need to be entered twice. Reports give founders a view of headcount and absence.

item.title: Culture Amp
item.description:
Culture Amp helps companies listen to employees. HR teams run engagement, onboarding, and exit surveys, analyze the results by team and demographic group, and compare against benchmarks from other organizations. Dashboards point out areas where scores are low and what drives them.

The platform also covers performance and development, with review cycles, goal tracking, and feedback. AI helps by summarizing open-ended comments into themes, drafting review text, and recommending actions to managers, which saves analysts days of reading. An assistant answers questions about results.

item.title: Factorial
item.description:
Factorial gathers HR tasks in one system. Companies store employee records, track attendance and time off, manage documents and contracts, run performance reviews, and handle recruiting and onboarding. Payroll is offered in several countries, and integrations connect with accounting and communication tools.

AI helps with administrative work. It can draft job descriptions and offer letters, answer employee questions about policies, and speed up payroll preparation. Reports give managers a view of headcount and absence.

item.title: Greenhouse
item.description: Greenhouse is an applicant tracking system for companies that want hiring to be systematic instead of ad hoc. Each job has a defined process: a posting, a set of stages, interview kits with questions, and scorecards that interviewers fill out against the same criteria. The aim is to reduce bias and gut-feel decisions by making every candidate go through the same structured steps. Recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers each get a view suited to their part of the work.

item.title: HiBob
item.description:
HiBob is built for companies that want a modern HR system for distributed teams. It stores employee records, handles onboarding and time off, supports performance reviews, and manages compensation and benefits. The interface is designed for employees as well as HR, with a social feel and company-wide features.

Analytics and AI help leaders. Compensation benchmarking compares pay with market data, workforce planning tools model headcount, and an assistant answers HR questions and drafts documents. Payroll integrations and a marketplace of apps connect Bob with finance and IT systems.

item.title: Lattice AI
item.description:
Lattice helps companies run performance and development programs. Managers and employees complete reviews and give continuous feedback, set goals and OKRs, hold one-on-ones with shared agendas, and track growth plans. Engagement surveys measure how employees feel, and compensation tools support pay reviews and planning, while an HR information system keeps employee records.

AI is added to reduce busywork. It can help managers draft feedback and review summaries, analyze survey comments for themes, and suggest talking points for one-on-ones. Insights flag possible retention risks or teams with low engagement, and an AI assistant answers questions about company data. The company has also launched products for managing AI agents as part of the workforce, a controversial idea.

item.title: Leapsome
item.description:
Leapsome gathers people processes in one product. HR teams run review cycles, set goals and OKRs, send engagement surveys, deliver learning content, and manage compensation planning, with the data connected so decisions draw on the full picture. It is used by mid-sized, often distributed companies.

AI helps with the heaviest reading and writing. It summarizes feedback, analyzes comments from surveys for sentiment and themes, helps managers draft reviews, and suggests development actions. Dashboards show trends by team.

item.title: Personio
item.description:
Personio centralizes HR work. Companies keep employee data, manage leave and attendance, handle recruiting from job posting to offer, prepare payroll, and run reviews, in one system designed around European employment rules. Self-service features let employees update their own data and request time off.

AI features help with common tasks. They draft job descriptions, assist with screening candidates, answer HR questions from company policy, and automate workflows. Reports show headcount, turnover, and other metrics.

item.title: Rippling
item.description:
Rippling combines employee data with the systems that depend on it. When a person joins, Rippling creates their payroll record, sets up benefits, provisions laptops and software accounts, and orders equipment, using one source of truth. Changes in the employee record cascade across the systems.

Modules cover HR, payroll in many countries, time and attendance, benefits, device and app management, and corporate cards and expenses. A workflow engine lets admins automate approvals and tasks, and AI assistants answer questions and draft content.

item.title: Workday
item.description:
Workday began as cloud HR software and expanded into financials. Large employers use it to keep employee records, run payroll and benefits, manage recruiting and performance, plan headcount and budgets, and close the books. Having HR and finance on one data model helps companies tie workforce decisions to costs.

AI shows up across the suite. It suggests candidates and skills matches, flags attrition risks, helps managers with planning, and drafts job descriptions and summaries. Workday has also introduced AI agents that take on tasks inside its apps, along with an agent management layer so that companies can control what those agents may do. It has bought AI companies to extend this, including some that build agent platforms.

item.title: Ashby
item.description:
Ashby brings together tools that recruiting teams often buy separately. The core is an applicant tracking system for jobs, candidates, and interview plans. Around it sit scheduling that coordinates interviewers automatically, a CRM for sourcing and nurturing talent, and an analytics layer that shows pipeline health, time to hire, and source effectiveness.

AI features handle repetitive work, such as summarizing candidates, drafting outreach, and taking notes in interviews. Structured scorecards and interview plans promote consistent evaluation, and reporting is built into the product rather than added on, which analytics-minded recruiting teams like.

item.title: Beamery
item.description:
Beamery treats talent like a relationship, not a one-off hire. Recruiters build pools of potential candidates, track interactions, run campaigns to stay in touch, and see who might fit upcoming roles. The same system can surface current employees for internal moves, which helps companies fill jobs from within.

Its AI builds around skills. It infers skills from resumes and profiles, maps them to a company’s roles, and recommends matches for jobs and development. Workforce planning tools help leaders see skill gaps and plan hiring or training. Integrations connect with applicant tracking systems such as Workday and SuccessFactors.

item.title: Gem
item.description:
Gem helps recruiting teams build pipelines. Recruiters search for candidates across LinkedIn and other sources, add them to talent pools, and send sequences of personalized outreach. A candidate CRM tracks every interaction, so when a role opens, the team can reach people they have already engaged.

Analytics show how sourcing channels perform, how long hiring takes, and where candidates drop out. AI features help with search, writing outreach, and identifying candidates who may be open to new roles. An applicant tracking system component extends the suite for teams that want everything in one place.

item.title: Paradox
item.description:
Paradox focuses on hiring for roles with many applicants, such as retail, hospitality, and logistics. Olivia chats with candidates by text or on a career site, asks qualifying questions, answers common questions about the job and company, and books interviews directly on managers’ calendars.

That removes much of the scheduling and screening back and forth that slows recruiting. Candidates get fast responses, and recruiters spend time on interviews instead of coordination. The platform includes an applicant tracking tool and onboarding support.

item.title: Phenom
item.description:
Phenom helps employers attract and manage talent. Its career sites show candidates jobs and content tailored to their interests, a recruiting CRM nurtures talent pools, and tools handle scheduling, chat, and applications. The same platform supports employees through internal job matching and career paths.

AI infers skills from resumes and profiles to match people with roles, recommend jobs, and surface candidates already in the system. Analytics show the hiring funnel and diversity data. The company sells to large enterprises.

item.title: SeekOut
item.description:
SeekOut builds a searchable database of professionals from public profiles and sources. Recruiters filter by skills, experience, and background, find candidates for roles like engineers and scientists, and reach out with outreach sequences.

AI helps match candidates to jobs and understand skill sets, and analytics show talent pools in a region or company. Diversity filters support recruiting programs, subject to legal rules on how they are used. Products extend to internal talent management for employers.

item.title: Eightfold AI
item.description:
Eightfold AI treats talent as a graph of skills. Its models read resumes, job descriptions, and employee profiles, infer skills, and match people to roles based on what they can do and are likely to learn, not just on keywords or job titles. Recruiters use it to find candidates in a company’s applicant database and external sources, and employees can see roles and learning paths that fit their skills.

The platform extends across the employee lifecycle. Modules cover talent acquisition, talent management, internal mobility, and workforce planning, with analytics that show skill gaps and diversity trends. Agent-style features automate steps such as screening and scheduling. It integrates with applicant tracking and HR systems such as Workday and SAP SuccessFactors.

item.title: HireVue
item.description:
HireVue lets candidates complete interviews on their own schedule. Employers set up structured questions, candidates record video answers, and recruiters review them later, which saves scheduling time when hiring many people. The platform has expanded to include game-based and skills assessments, live interviews, text-based chat for scheduling and screening, and tools for coding interviews.

Its use of AI has been controversial. HireVue once analyzed facial expressions and voice in interviews, which drew criticism from privacy and civil rights groups, and it dropped facial analysis. Today it describes using structured scoring based on what candidates say and on job-relevant skills, and publishes audits and explanations of its models. Regulations in places such as New York City and Illinois now require notice, consent, or bias audits for automated hiring tools.
